label: rem:collatz-surreal-bound
title: Surreal bound for Collatz: contact-boundary deviation costs transfinite Reeb period
html:
Remark. Surreal bound for Collatz: contact-boundary deviation costs transfinite Reeb period

We translate the contact-boundary argument of the q-Collatz conjecture (q-Collatz, Collatz no cycles) into a literal surreal inequality in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon).

Let \varepsilon \in \mathrm{Der}(A) be the Reeb infinitesimal (Reeb infinitesimal) and q = 1 + \varepsilon (q from \varepsilon). The q-Collatz conjecture translates the integer orbit into a skein-module resolution on the Reeb contact boundary. A rogue orbit is a non-trivial cycle or an unbounded hailstone. The rogue drift \delta measures the excess contact volume produced per step.

The Reeb period of the contact boundary is \Omega_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-1} (surreal rate calculus). A standard-real drift \delta > 0 per step produces an accumulated contact-volume deviation over one Reeb period:

V(\delta) \asymp \delta^2 \cdot \Omega_q \asymp \delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon^{-1}

The mass-gap dissipation available to re-absorb the deviation is \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3. By surreal squeeze, \delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon^{-1} > \varepsilon^3 strictly in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon). Hence:

V(\delta) > \Delta_q \qquad (\text{in } \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon) \subset \mathbf{No}).

Equivalently, \ordw(V(\delta)) = 1 > -3 = \ordw(\Delta_q) in the \omega-adic order of Big-O via \ordw.

No rogue orbit with standard-real drift \delta > 0 can persist. The Reeb period sweeps a contact-volume transfinite larger than the mass-gap infinitesimal. No budget exists to dissipate the accumulated excess. This is the surreal-arithmetic form of the q-Collatz conjecture, consistent with Collatz no cycles.

The classical Collatz orbit on \mathbb{N} is the standard part \mathrm{st}\bigl(\cdot \,|_{q = 1 + \varepsilon}\bigr) of the q-deformed skein resolution (calculus up to \varepsilon). Every infinitesimal drift vanishes under \mathrm{st}. Every standard-real drift is prohibited by the squeeze above. Therefore, \mathrm{st}(\delta) = 0 for every admissible surreal drift. All orbits terminate at 1.

The q-Collatz statement upgrades to a surreal inequality that rules out all standard-real drifts. We recover the classical conjecture only by assuming the q-Collatz skein-module resolution admits a well-defined standard part.
